title: [bug] Every remaining D1 Worker call 401s — no account row is ever created
description:
Found by audit 2026-08-13. THE SINGLE ROOT CAUSE behind most broken journeys.

api.createAccount was migrated to fire.ensureIdentity, so nothing in the client calls POST /accounts any more. That route is what creates the D1 'accounts' row. server/src/auth.ts:231-239 looks the caller up by firebase_uid and returns {class:'stranger'} when there is no row; requirePlayer (auth.ts:278-281) then fails 401 'Open the link you were sent, or sign in.'

The Firebase project matches on both sides, so the token verifies fine — the account simply does not exist in D1. Net effect: EVERY remaining Worker call returns a 401 telling an already-signed-in person to sign in. That is the string appearing on Play, Propose and Record.

15 of 40 api.ts methods still route to the Worker. Those with live callers, by visibility:
1. startSession (play.tsx:242) — Play tab's primary action for any night without a printed lineup.
2. createGroup (start.tsx:94) — every new user's FIRST action, and start.tsx:115 maps the 401 to 'you are not signed in', so the user is looped through sign-in forever.
3. proposeEvent (propose.tsx:67) — no new games can be created.
4. recordMatch (record.tsx:116) — standalone score entry never persists.
5. severPreview/severAccount (you.tsx:313/:305) — 'Delete everything' does nothing at all, no try/catch and Button's onPress is () => void so the rejection is unhandled. This is the APPLE-MANDATED ACCOUNT DELETION PATH.
6. claimPreview/claimAccept (claim/[token].tsx:53/:62) — every claim link renders as expired, because :55 swallows the failure into setGone(true).
7. getSession/commitRound/closeSession (live-session.tsx:42/212/217) — session resume hangs on LOADING forever; the round buttons do nothing.

TWO ROUTES: (a) BRIDGE — restore account provisioning so the Worker paths work again until migrated. Cheap, unblocks 6 journeys today, but invests in the backend being retired. (b) MIGRATE each to Firestore. Correct, larger. Recommend deciding before touching any of them.

Dead Worker methods with no callers, safe to delete: resolveInvite, joinByInvite, ledger, createSeries (plus the MOCK export, InviteView/JoinResult types and DEMO_INVITE/demoJoin fixtures).
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-13 by querying production D1 directly. The mechanism in the description is right; the BLAST RADIUS as first written was wrong.

D1 holds: 1 account, 56 players. The single account is acc_01kzwn2bwf8wnm4vy4mpd4wq3t, firebase_uid agXrxlKGXibDduj8DWMeJxFUO8E3 (the owner's), status active, linked to player plr_founder 'John' — seeded, not created by the client.

So requirePlayer RESOLVES for the owner and the Worker journeys were most likely NOT broken for him. The audit inferred the 401 from reading the code path, not from exercising it. Everybody who is NOT the founder — all 55 other players, and every future sign-up — has no account row and would 401.

BRIDGE SHIPPED 53982fa (deployed): api.createAccount calls POST /accounts again, and api.ensureWorkerAccount is fired unawaited from restoreSignIn so an ALREADY signed-in session gets the row too (adopt() only runs on the sign-in buttons, so without that second call the fix would reach nobody already here). Both best-effort and silent — Firestore is the identity the app runs on and a retired Worker must not block sign-in. Server route is idempotent (returns early when the account already has a player), so the founder cannot be given a second one.

STILL OPEN, and this issue stays open for it: the 15 Worker-routed methods themselves. The bridge buys time; it does not migrate them. Also unverified — whether startSession/proposeEvent/recordMatch actually succeed end to end now for a fresh account. Nobody has exercised them against the live Worker.

title: [bug] Every game involving the unfilled #16 seat was dropped by the vegas import — 35 matches missing from Saturday alone
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while chasing uneven game counts in the league table. This is the cause, and it is NOT a sub rule.

THE ARITHMETIC. Saturday Adv 4.0-4.5 has 5 played weeks x 7 games x 4 courts = 28 matches a week, 140 in total. Firestore holds 105 — exactly 21 a week. Counting the scoresheets: 140 matches, of which 35 involve seat #16, leaving 105. The import has precisely the 105 that do not touch #16, in all five weeks, with no exceptions.

WHY. Seat #16 was never filled, so a different sub plays it every week (Mike Wong, Jessica Flores, Nive Isabel, Darrick Publow). None of them has a players/ record, so import_vegas_bulk could not resolve the id and dropped the whole match rather than the one player.

WHAT IT BREAKS. Every player's totals are short by however often they shared a court with #16 — the table shows 24-30 games where all fifteen should read 35, and points are short to match (Melissa Lacro reads 255 against the workbook's 298; Brian Judkins 272 against 348). The league table in the app is wrong for everybody, in different amounts.

THE OWNER'S READ was that the uneven counts come from subs and want an asterisk plus a footnote. The instinct is right — subs ARE why — but an asterisk here would dress a missing-import bug as a league rule, and the numbers would stay wrong underneath it. Fix the import first, then the asterisk marks the seats the workbook actually marks.

FIX: mint a player per sub (or one per league for the standing seat, if the city treats #16 as a seat rather than a person — the workbook writes the sub's real name into the #16 row each week, which argues for real people), then re-import the 35 missing Saturday matches and whatever the equivalent is on Thursday. Check Thursday too: 140 matches present against 5 weeks x 28 = 140 expected, so it may be complete — its #15/#16 seats were filled.

Then verify against the workbook's Weekly Scoring totals, which are authoritative: every player should read 35 games, and season points should match the Weekly Standings overall column.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-08-13. scripts/import_vegas_missing_seat_matches.ts (Billers commit afa8c0c) wrote the 35 missing Saturday matches — 7 per week, every game seat #16 was drawn into. All fifteen members now read 35 games (5 weeks x 7) where they had read 24-30. Attributed to the people the scoresheet names in the #16 row (Mike Wong wk1+wk5, Jessica Flores wk2+wk4, Nive Isabel wk3), all three of whom already existed in players/. Deduped on the four playerIds + week + court rather than the game number, because 55 of the imported matches say 'Game ?' and a game-number key would have double-written 85 present matches. Thursday needed nothing: 140 present against 140 on the scoresheets (its week 1 genuinely has 26 games, not 28). Points now agree exactly with the city's standings for every player whose seat was never subbed; the seven that differ are the cap, tracked separately.

title: There is no way to drop out of an event on any screen
description: Found by three independent persona reviews of design/journeys (beginner, rec organiser, league organiser). The entire product philosophy rests on withdrawal being free and cheap: RosterEntry.state has 'dropped', the cascade invariants describe sponsor drops removing three people from two courts, INV-4 promotion exists to fill the gap, and a recorded design constraint says a player's name must never be rendered next to failure language BECAUSE dropping out early is the single most valuable social behaviour in the product. Not one screen in 111 lets anybody leave. rec-friends/2's only button is 'I'm in'. home/1 prints 'Are you playing / they need an answer' with exactly one button. entry/2 says 'Nothing to do - see you at 8.' The beginner persona's verdict: 'joining is one tap and leaving is invisible. That's not free, that's a trap door I can't find' - and she said she would text the organiser rather than open the app. This also blocks the promotion/relay journey, which cannot be drawn without a drop to trigger it.
acceptance_criteria: An event screen shows how to withdraw, the withdrawal screen carries no fault language, and the cascade + promotion that follows is drawn including the sponsor relay.
close_reason: Closed

title: DUPR: partner API is the only legitimate path — apply, and design DUPR as optional
description:
Research 2026-08-13. Owner wants to pull friends match history from DUPR so an invited friend arrives to a real profile rather than an empty one.

FEASIBLE, BUT ONLY AS A PARTNER.

WHAT EXISTS:
- A PARTNER API, and it does exactly what is wanted. Base https://api.dupr.com/api (UAT https://uat.mydupr.com/api), authenticated with a partner client key + secret exchanged for a token. Documented endpoints include get ratings by DUPR ID, GET DUPR ID BY EMAIL, search users, SEARCH MATCH HISTORY (filter by DUPR ID, date range, singles/doubles), club match search, and webhooks with RATING and MATCH topics. Evidenced by a third-party PHP SDK (github.com/Info-Esportes/dupr-partner-api) pointing at DUPR own swagger, plus DUPR own API Partners PDF listing CourtReserve, Playbypoint, PodPlay, Swish, Scoreholio and others, and github.com/myDUPR webhookExampleProject.
- A docs portal at https://api.dupr.gg/api-explorer?group=public splitting Public (external read-only tokens) from Internal (staff only). NOT VERIFIED — it is a JS app the researcher could not render. WORTH TEN MINUTES IN A BROWSER; it could change the whole answer.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT: dupr.com/terms, effective 2025-09-24, prohibits users from using "spiders, crawlers, robots, scrapers, automated tools"; from "data scraping, web scraping, web harvesting, web data extraction"; from downloading or archiving "any substantial portion"; and licenses use for "non-commercial, internal business or personal use". That rules out the undocumented backend.mydupr.com route that every hobby project uses, AND rules out asking a friend for their DUPR login. Do not ship either.

NO CONSENT FLOW EXISTS. The partner API is two-legged — partner credentials only, keyed on DUPR ID or email, with no per-player authorization step. Player "linking" in existing partner apps is the player typing their DUPR ID, which is an identifier and not a grant. So consent is handled contractually, not technically, and that is a question for DUPR.

FIRST STEPS, in parallel: (1) open the api-explorer public group in a browser and see what a read-only token actually gets; (2) email support@mydupr.com for partner onboarding — describe the app, the read use case, ask about terms, fees and the consent model. Expect them to care most about whether we also WRITE verified results back, since that is what every listed partner does.

MEANWHILE, AND THIS IS THE PART TO BUILD NOW: design DUPR as an enhancement, never a dependency. Let somebody enter their DUPR ID, show it as SELF-REPORTED, and deep-link to their public DUPR profile. That delivers most of the enticement with zero legal exposure and drops in cleanly behind a real partner integration later. It also fits the existing decision that this app does not show unearned ratings (see the rating issue, and the memory on Billers 1200/1500 Elo defaults).

title: Every section shouts equally: one display head per screen, and give the screens a Hero
description:
Visual hierarchy review 2026-08-13. This is the mechanical cause of "just placed on there".

COUNTED. Home (index.tsx) has 3 SectionHeads (:74, :174, :213) plus an Empty whose title is ALSO displayLg (kitchenline.tsx:252) plus type.display used as body at :80, :91 and :179 — six display-weight elements and ZERO giant numerals. Groups has 3 in the multi-group case (:133, :175, :255), and :133/:175 print the group name TWICE within ~100px.

Hero is imported on neither screen — only propose.tsx:115 and edit/[id].tsx:163. So Home does exactly what kitchenline.tsx:326-333 warns against: it states its number in a sentence (event.fill.message, :91) instead of showing it.

CHANGES, in order:
1. Give each screen a Hero and take the headline away from everything else. Home: collapse :74 + :87-92 into one Hero, numeral = the fill count. Groups: collapse :133 into a Hero, numeral = member count — today that count only renders when groups.length > 1 (:175), so the owner with one group NEVER SEES A NUMBER AT ALL.
2. Empty must never follow a SectionHead. group.tsx:113->116 stacks two displayLg headlines 7px apart on the same surface; same at :247->248. Add an optional note prop to Empty so it renders its own head, and delete the SectionHead above it.
3. Standings must not outrank the roster. group.tsx:247-251 gives a full display headline plus 30 words about a denominator to a table that will not exist for weeks, while the actual member list gets a bare 11px eyebrow (:311). Largest hierarchy inversion on either screen.
4. Extract a SubHead primitive (eyebrow + hairline, no display type) and use it for the four quiet peers — WHEN IT PLAYS (:199), IN THE GROUP (:311), standings (:255), and Home last-result/after-that (:174, :213). Right now two get a bare eyebrow with a CLOSING hairline, so the rule reads as belonging to the block below it.
5. Vertical rhythm is three different gaps between top-level blocks in group.tsx: space.lg (:174, :246, :254), space.md (:198, :310) and a bare marginTop:4 (:187). Pick space.lg between sections, space.sm inside a composition, nothing else.
6. Stop floating padded content on the ground. ground and surface are ~1.2:1 apart — invisible as a separator — yet the two primary CTAs sit on bare ground with no surface, no rule, no edge (index.tsx:140, group.tsx:225). That IS the "plonked in the middle". Put them on a surface bounded by hairlines, or make the invite a full-bleed Ask.
7. CourtPlate is 100% width and lands between two padded blocks with no rule on either edge, so it reads as an image dropped in rather than a plate set into the page.

TWO GRAMMAR LEAKS: index.tsx:203 prints a hyphenated score on one line, the exact thing kitchenline.tsx:180-192 refuses to provide an API for. index.tsx:179-184 sets a single W/L letter in type.display; a record mark is a datum and belongs in mono.

title: Ghost buttons are invisible in sunlight, and on the destructive screens they are the safe option
description:
Accessibility review 2026-08-13. Context: played outdoors in Las Vegas, one-handed, often by players in their 60s-70s.

THE GOOD NEWS FIRST, verified by computing the ratios: every TEXT pair in app/src/theme/tokens.ts:43-155 passes WCAG AA. fg2 on surface 7.92:1, fg3 on surface 6.42:1, onBall on ball 10.90:1, ballInk on light stock 6.78:1. Nothing text-bearing is below 4.5:1. The palette is the strongest part of the design.

THE FAILURE IS NON-TEXT CONTRAST (WCAG 1.4.11, needs 3:1):
- rule #24606F on deck1 = 1.97:1. Light mode ruleL on stock = 1.52:1.
- Button ghost (kitchenline.tsx:104-105) has NO FILL — its entire affordance is a 1px c.rule border. In sun it is an invisible rectangle.
- CONSEQUENCE, and this is why it is P1: on the drop-out and remove-player screens (event/[id].tsx:549-553, :767-771) the cancel option is a ghost and the destructive option is an Ask in ball yellow. Outdoors the ONLY VISIBLE BUTTON IS THE DESTRUCTIVE ONE.
- Every list separator is that same 1px rule, so roster rows visually merge outdoors — bad when row ORDER is the product's core mechanic.
- CourtPlate names are 13px (kitchenline.tsx:413), below the file's own stated 15px body floor, on the most-glanced element on a court.

ALSO: zero accessibilityRole/Label/State anywhere in app/ (grep returns nothing). Eight <Text onPress> sites are real actions that become non-focusable spans on RN Web — unreachable by keyboard, unannounced by VoiceOver: roster removal (event/[id].tsx:483), WHOLE SCHEDULE ROWS (schedule.tsx:98-105, so the Schedule tab has no operable controls on web), group night rows (group.tsx:204-207), Insights player rows (numbers.tsx:164-166), timezone change (start.tsx:187, ~13pt), and four inline-name sites at ~19pt. No hitSlop anywhere. Score numerals on the plate are 34pt — the mid-session, paddle-in-hand tap.

FIX ORDER: (1) give Button ghost a real fill or a ruleHard border and raise separators to 3:1; (2) convert the eight Text onPress sites to Pressable with role+label, minHeight 44; (3) move the removal confirmation next to its row — today the toggle, the trigger and the confirmation are three separate scroll positions and never co-visible on a 16-person roster; (4) theme override at you.tsx:327 is plain useState, so a player who forces LIGHT for the sun re-forces it every cold start.

title: Home is a single-event detail screen, not a gateway
description:
UX review 2026-08-13, owner: "Everything on Home seems like it is just placed on there. I think that is because originally that is what Play was. This should be the gateway to the other sections and it seems a bit too heavily focused on the next event."

CONFIRMED BY GIT: commit 92459ad ("Five tabs, and the bar never leaves") took index.tsx 620 -> 256 lines and created play.tsx at 191. Home was TRUNCATED, not re-conceived. Its own header comment (index.tsx:1-14) states the intended job — "is anything waiting on me?" — and no code implements it.

TODAY: everything above the fold reads ONE object, home.next_event, five ways (fill line :87-92, court plate :97-134, CTA :140-149). home.groups is used only as a boolean (:56); home.upcoming only as a count (:211-213).

WORSE THAN IT LOOKS: next is upcoming[0] (firedata.ts:315), so a null next_event IMPLIES upcoming is empty — the "AFTER THAT" block cannot render either. On a no-game day Home is an eyebrow, an Empty, maybe a last result, and two ghost buttons. That is six days out of seven for a Thursday league.

FIRST CHANGE: delete the court plate from Home (index.tsx:97-134). ~40 lines, zero data work. It duplicates play.tsx:280-305 against the same data — Play own comment admits it ("the same plate the night and Home draw", play.tsx:278-279) — and Home copy goes stale the moment game 1 ends because Play tracks the played set and Home does not. Two screens, one fact, one of them wrong.

THEN, and three of these need NO new data:
- "Needs you": events in the grouped query but not the rostered query are exactly the nights you have not answered. Both sets are already in memory in home() (firedata.ts:279-296). Zero new reads.
- Which upcoming nights are SHORT: toEventView already computes fill.needed and fill.spare (:220-230) but home() only calls it for the next event (:319). The EventDocs are already in byId.
- Promote home.groups to a rendered section — it is fetched (:264-273) and thrown away.
- NEEDS BUILDING: scores awaiting confirmation does not exist (recordLineupGame writes a confirmed status unconditionally, firedata.ts:1328); standings MOVEMENT needs snapshots.

DEAD CODE FOUND ALONGSIDE: live_session_id is hardcoded null (firedata.ts:260, :329) and in demo (api.ts:174), so the live-session banner at index.tsx:78-83 can NEVER render, and play.tsx:69 branches on the same constant. unseen_match_id (firedata.ts:330) is read by nothing. home.hero (:317) is computed and never consumed. Wire them or delete them.

title: DECISION: no sub-tabs inside Groups — the deck already rules on this
description:
Owner asked 2026-08-13: 'Maybe introducing a tab system might be better.' Two reviewers disagreed; the design deck settles it.

AGAINST (recommended):
- app/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:2-3 and design/journeys/README.md:12-15 state the governing law: 'the tab bar selects a scope, never a feature.' Sub-tabs inside Groups select a feature within a scope, and put two tab bars ~60px apart.
- design/prototype-kitchenline/08-shapes.html:1446 treats any switcher as CHROME, to be paid for only when data forces it: 'A switcher is chrome, and most people have exactly one group.'
- Volume does not justify it. Whitney Ranch Crew is 1 member, 4 nights, 0 standings rows — about 8 rows total. Sub-tabs earn their keep when panes overflow a viewport; here two of three panes are EMPTY.
- It hides the motivating state: for a 1-person group the point is that the roster is nearly empty, and a tab buries the exact fact that should trigger the invite.

WHAT THE DECK DOES SANCTION: a segmented control exists (design/journeys/index.html:1133-1137, re-skinned :853-876) and is used twice — to SET A VALUE (invite_mode, visibility tier, event intent) and to FILTER ONE LIST (All/Doubles/Singles at :2052). Never to navigate between sections. So a switcher is available vocabulary, just not for this job.

CONSEQUENCE: fix Groups by reordering (see the Groups issue), not by adding panes.

STILL WORTH DOING from the navigation review: extract ONE in-screen switching primitive so the app stops having four selection grammars (ghost-button pair at event/[id].tsx:332-335, pager dots, group.tsx's left ball inset, the tab bar's dash). Proposed rule: named alternatives -> a 'Faces' component styled as the tab bar's inverse (dash BELOW the label); ordered sequence -> pager with dots; picking a subject -> the left-inset list row. Then retire event/[id].tsx:332-335 into it.

title: Groups: put the people and the invite together, and drop the third page title
description:
UX review 2026-08-13, owner's complaint: 'you should be able to see who's in them and invite people linked together... they're all separate sections and events are just plonked in the middle.'

DIAGNOSIS. Three SectionHeads on one scroll, each closed by a 3px hard baseline = three severed regions: 'Your groups' (group.tsx:133), the group name (:176), and 'No games recorded' (:247). Meanwhile WHEN IT PLAYS (:199) and IN THE GROUP (:311) are 11px eyebrows with no baseline — so a permanently-empty standings block OUTRANKS the member list typographically. The header note says '{n} IN · {n} BROUGHT' (:175), a membership fact, then immediately renders the schedule; the promise is paid off four sections later.

SUB-TABS: RECOMMENDED AGAINST — see the separate decision issue. Fix the order instead.

FIRST CHANGE (~10 lines moved, 7 deleted, no new component): move the invite block (:225-231) to be the LAST ROW of the members list (:234-236), and delete the duplicate SectionHead (:173-179). Second: gate :245 on rows.length > 0 so the screen stops ending on a permanent dead end.

THEN: leagues need a different body. members(leagueId) reads groups/{id}, which does not exist for a city league (firedata.ts:1418-1421), so the header reads '0 IN · 0 BROUGHT' for a 15-person league — factually false — and the invite button still mints a working /join/{leagueId} link into a league the owner cannot administer. The client already has both signals and reads neither: the 20-hex kind regex (:165) and people.you.role (firedata.ts:1052-1055). League body should be: nights first, one WHERE YOU STAND row pushing to /standings/{id}, no invite, and a stamp saying the city runs it.

title: Play tab: promotion is promised and never delivered, live session cannot resume
description:
Audit 2026-08-13.

(1) dropPreview (firedata.ts:409-444) promises 'N PEOPLE GET TOLD' and names who gets promoted; event/[id].tsx:711-731 renders it. Promotion itself is implicit in toEventView's slice math, which is fine — but NO NOTIFICATION IS EMITTED. fire.nudge has zero callers in app/, and functions/src/index.ts only has onNudge (fed by those uncalled docs) and the scheduled reminder. There is no roster-change trigger. The preview's central promise is unbacked.

(2) firedata.ts:329 hardcodes live_session_id: null in the production home() response. So play.tsx:62 can never restore a session — sessionId is otherwise only set by startSession and is plain component state. Kill the app mid rec-morning and the session is unrecoverable. index.tsx:78-83's 'A session is on right now' card is unreachable code in production AND in demo.

(3) app/app/session/[id].tsx is an orphan: nothing navigates to it, and push.ts installs no notification-response handler, so no notification can route there either. Its onDone diverges from the tab's (navigates to / vs refresh in place).

title: Writes across the app swallow their own failures
description:
Audit 2026-08-13. The reason 'Take off' was invisible for so long, and it is systemic rather than one screen.

app/src/components/kitchenline.tsx:81,97 — Ask and Button take onPress?: () => void and hand it straight to Pressable. Any async handler's rejection is unhandled and produces NO UI change at all. That is what makes you.tsx:313 (severPreview) and live-session.tsx:212/217 (commitRound, closeSession) buttons that do literally nothing when they fail.

Event screen mutations use try/finally with no catch: confirmDrop ([id].tsx:155), join (:167), bringGuest (:186). removeThem was fixed in c8c7b15; the others were not.

claim/[token].tsx:55 — .catch(() => setGone(true)) renders ANY failure as 'this link is expired'.
live-session.tsx:42 — refresh() has no .catch, so a failed getSession leaves the screen on LOADING forever.

api.ts:101-107 — call() collapses any non-JSON failure into a fabricated {code:'not_found', message:'We could not find that.'}. A 5xx, a gateway page and a real 404 are indistinguishable. The true status survives on .status but only record.tsx:130 and start.tsx:115 read it.

WANTED: make Ask/Button accept () => void | Promise<void> and handle rejection, or require callers to catch; give the event screen the same error surface removeThem now has; stop claim from reporting failure as expiry.

title: The coverage report has nowhere to be read — in-app half of reminders
description:
The send path (pickleball-social 9b8ecac) writes schedule_events/{id}.lastReminder = {at, why, summary, told[], missed[{playerId,name,why}], failed}. Nothing in the app displays it.

That matters because the channel decision was IN-APP + PUSH, and push alone will not cover this crowd — the whole reason the report distinguishes needs_home_screen from never_asked is so the organiser can see WHO to chase by other means. A report only visible in Cloud Functions logs does not do that.

WANTED on the event screen, organiser-only: the last reminder's summary line, and the missed list by name with the reason in plain words ('Jimbo — never opened the app', 'Marco — iOS, needs the app on his home screen'). Plus the nudge button itself, which does not exist in the UI yet: firedata.nudge(eventId, onlyPlayerId?) is written and now delivered, but nothing calls it.

Also worth surfacing the same thing for the person who is unreachable: if you are signed in on iOS in a browser tab, the app can tell you that you will not get reminders and what to do about it. push.ts already detects needs_home_screen.

title: Whitney reminders: the send path and the scheduled trigger
description:
Owner sequenced this AFTER editable rec events (done, ac5164b) and after device registration (done, de03bb3). This is the remaining half.

WHAT EXISTS NOW:
- Device tokens write to Firestore on join: users/{uid}.pushToken (the field Billers' six notifiers already read) plus a users/{uid}.devices map carrying platform, permission, webInstallState, reachable and failure per device. See fire.registerDevice.
- firedata.nudge(eventId, onlyPlayerId?) appends to schedule_events/{id}/nudges. The write exists; nothing delivers it.
- Billers has admin.messaging().send() in pickleball_stats/functions — see src/ratingMilestoneNotifier.js and src/referralRewardNotifier.js for the established buildFcmMessage shape.

WHAT IS LEFT:
(a) A trigger on schedule_events/{id}/nudges/{nudgeId} that resolves the event's roster -> playerIds -> users docs -> pushToken, and sends. That is the MANUAL nudge button delivered.
(b) A scheduled function that fires before every rec game regardless of numbers (owner's call: ALWAYS auto-remind). Needs a per-event marker so a reminder is not sent twice, and it must skip league nights.
(c) THE COVERAGE REPORT, which the owner explicitly wanted: the send must return who could NOT be reached, not just a success count. The devices map is what makes this answerable — an entry with reachable:false and failure:'needs_home_screen' is a specific, explainable person, not a silent gap. Reaching four of twelve and reporting success is the failure mode to avoid.
(d) An in-app surface for the same thing, since 'in-app + push' was the channel decision and push alone will not cover this crowd.

BLOCKED ON A DECISION, not on code: this deploys Cloud Functions into the live Billers project and sends real notifications to real people. Do not deploy without the owner saying so.

NOTE the iOS ceiling: web push needs the app added to the home screen. push.ts detects it (needs_home_screen) and registerDevice now records it, so coverage can be measured BEFORE the first send — worth doing, because if it is 3 of 12 the owner said to revisit SMS/Telegram.

title: Whitney rec games: editable, with automatic reminders and a manual nudge
description:
Owner 2026-08-13. The particular problem: confirming numbers for the Sunday Whitney Ranch rec game, and finding the balance between reminders that fire themselves and a nudge he sends when he wants one.

WANTED: the rec events editable (time, place, capacity, note), plus notifications to remind people about a game or ask them to join.

DECISIONS (owner, 2026-08-13):
- CHANNEL: in-app + push.
- CADENCE: ALWAYS auto-remind before every game regardless of numbers, AND a manual nudge button on top.

PREREQUISITE, and it blocks the channel choice: push does not currently work against the live backend. api.registerDevice posts to the D1 Worker (POST /devices), which is the backend being retired, and there is no Firestore-side device registry or send path. So this needs (a) device tokens stored in Firestore, (b) a send path — Billers already has messaging_send_message via FCM and functions/index.js has FCM triggers, so the pieces exist on that side, and (c) a scheduled trigger for the automatic reminder.

Also note what push cannot reach: anybody without an account and without the app added to their home screen (iOS web push requires it — push.ts already detects and reports needs_home_screen). For the Whitney crowd that may be most of them, so the first send should report who could not be reached rather than silently reaching four people out of twelve. title: Play: quick entry — log a game with anyone, share one claim link per game
description:
Owner 2026-08-13. Play offers a second door beside the scheduled events: LOG A GAME, no event required.

FLOW: pick a court -> pick players from people you already know, or type a name for somebody new -> enter the score on the plate -> record. Then either NEXT GAME (the session rolls on, re-pick or rotate) or SHARE, which produces a QR code and a copyable link.

ONE LINK PER GAME. If three players were unregistered they all get the SAME link; each opens it and picks which of the unclaimed names is theirs. That claims the spot and everything attached to it.

DECISIONS (owner, 2026-08-13):
- CLAIMING REQUIRES A REAL SIGN-IN (Google/Apple), consistent with the anonymous-auth reversal. The spot and its games move onto an account that can be reached and corrected later. app/claim/[token].tsx is the existing UX reference and already does sign-in-for-claim (signInWithAppleForClaim / signInWithGoogleWebForClaim).
- UNCLAIMED GAMES COUNT FOR THE PEOPLE WHO ARE REAL, AND ARE HELD FOR THE ONE WHO IS NOT. The owner's record updates the moment he records; the typed-name side sits unclaimed and attaches retroactively on claim. Do NOT mint a speculative player doc per typed name — that creates people who may never exist and are painful to merge (see the five John twins).

OPEN: the match doc shape for a held side. Billers' matches want playerIds on both teams; a name with no id has nowhere to live. Options: a pending-claims collection keyed to the match, or a player doc flagged unclaimed with a claim token. The second reuses the existing claim door but is the thing the decision above warns about — resolve before building.

Depends on nothing shipped; the plate scoring, CourtPager and recordLineupGame are all in place and this is a second caller of them.
notes:
DECIDED (owner, 2026-08-13, second pass): the held side lives in a PENDING-CLAIMS COLLECTION, not an unclaimed player doc. Shape:

matches/{id}
  team1PlayerIds: [realIds...]     // only people who actually exist
  team2PlayerIds: [realIds...]
  pendingSeats: <count>            // so the match knows it is incomplete

pending_claims/{token}
  matchIds: [...]                  // ONE token spans the whole session — one link per game as specced, and a session shares it
  seats: [{ team: 1|2, name: 'Marco', claimedBy: null }]

Claiming resolves a seat: real sign-in, pick which unclaimed name is yours, then the name moves out of pending and the playerId is appended to the match's team array. Nothing speculative is ever written into players/.

Consequence to handle: recomputeLeagueStats and any stats reader must tolerate a match whose teams are short a player. Verify before writing the claim path.

title: Show the sub cap rather than just applying it
description:
Owner 2026-08-13: 'I think those rules are in there but we can probably visually show it and make the rules clear a bit more.'

The cap is about to become invisible arithmetic — a player's total will silently differ from the sum of their game scores, which is exactly the kind of number that makes people distrust a table. It has to explain itself where it lands.

Where it lands:
- THE TABLE: a row whose total was capped carries a mark, and the mark has a footnote in the league's own words — 'a sub played your seat in weeks 2 and 4; a subbed seat scores at most 7 a game'. This is the asterisk the owner asked for, and it belongs on the CAPPED row, not on the sub.
- THE LEDGER / a game: a game where the seat was capped should show both numbers rather than one — the team scored 11, the seat took 7. Hiding the real score would be worse than showing the cap.
- THE PLAYER PAGE of a sub: they scored what they scored. Nothing here caps their own record, and the page should not imply the league ranks them, because it does not.

Wording rule, from the deck: the cap is a fact about a SEAT and a season's fairness, never a mark against a person. 'Subbed seat — 7 a game' not 'penalised'.

Scope note: the rule is confirmed for City of Las Vegas and Excel. Do NOT write copy asserting it is a pickleball-wide standard — the owner does not know that it is, and a made-up universal is the kind of thing that ends up quoted back. Keep it attributed to the league, which also makes it correct when a league without the rule shows up.
close_reason: Shipped in pickleball-social ea087ed. Asterisk on the name of any capped row; underneath it one line per affected week — 'NIVE PLAYED WK1 · 54 → 39' — carrying BOTH figures, because a capped total does not match the sum of that person's game scores and a number you cannot reproduce is a number people stop believing. Where the scoresheet marked a seat subbed but never named who, it says 'a sub' rather than inventing one. The rule sits once at the foot of the table, attributed to the league rather than asserted as a pickleball standard, and worded as a fact about a SEAT — the sub keeps what they scored on their own record.

title: Guest join by first name is impossible against Firestore — foundation 1 needs a callable
description:
Blocking foundation 1 (a link and a first name is the whole of it, no account required), which the D1 guest door used to deliver and the Firestore one cannot.

players/ is admin-write-only in Billers' firestore.rules, so a client cannot mint a player from a name typed by a stranger. createPlayer (functions/index.js ~424) and createGuestPlayer (~476) both require context.auth, so they do not help an anonymous visitor either.

Options: (a) enable Firebase ANONYMOUS auth, so the invite door signs the visitor in anonymously and then calls createPlayer — the account is real to Firestore, invisible to the person, and upgradeable later by linking a Google/Apple credential to the same uid (this is the standard path and preserves the record when they do sign in properly); (b) a new unauthenticated callable that takes {groupId, displayName} plus App Check and mints a player + roster slot, which reopens the abuse surface the admin-write-only rule was closing; (c) accept sign-in as the price of entry and drop foundation 1, which is a product decision, not an implementation one.

(a) is the recommendation. Note the app already has App Check setup docs in pickleball_stats.

Until this lands, app/join/[token].tsx asks for sign-in and says so in plain words.

title: Extend submitMatchScore so it can express a league game (leagueId, real playedAt, ties, round-robin dedupe)
description:
Found while building wr0. The callable is the preferred write channel (server validation, Admin SDK) but as written it CANNOT record a city league game, which is why Golden Pickle writes matches directly instead (see recordLineupGame in pickleball-social/app/src/lib/firedata.ts and the rules' isMatchSafeCreate).

Four gaps in pickleball_stats/functions/index.js submitMatchScore (~line 531):
1. NO leagueId. It writes scopeType/scopeId/groupId only. Every imported league match carries leagueId, and firedata's MyMatch reads leagueId to split league from rec — so a game scored through the callable lands in the REC denominator. That silently rots the league/rec split the entire stats spec is built on.
2. playedAt = new Date() server-now, with a comment admitting the uncertainty. A score entered on the drive home, or a night entered the next morning, gets the wrong date; the ledger and 'recent' order by it.
3. validateScore rejects ties (team1Score === team2Score returns false). Timed city games finish level when the horn goes — the imported data has ties, which is why Insights prints '· N tied'. A real tied league game cannot be submitted.
4. Dedupe checksum is day + sorted players + score. A round robin has you meeting the same four people more than once in a morning; a second 11-9 between the same pair is refused as 'already-exists'. Needs a caller-supplied idempotency key (eventId+game+court) instead.

Suggested signature additions: leagueId, playedAt (validated 'not in the distant future'), allowTie when scopeType==='league', and idempotencyKey replacing/augmenting the checksum. Once shipped, switch recordLineupGame over and delete the direct-write path with its long comment.

Note the write shape to match: team1PlayerIds/team2PlayerIds/team1Score/team2Score/format/scopeType/scopeId/leagueId/status/playedAt/playedOn/date/court/gameNumber/tag/location.

title: Subs are invisible: name the sub, mark them (S), and count against the 7-appearance cap
description:
Owner 2026-08-13. Three facts the app currently cannot express.

(1) THE STANDING SUB. Saturday Adv 4.0-4.5 has never filled its 16th spot — a sub has taken that seat all season. Today the roster just shows 15 in and 'COURT 4 - FORMING', and whoever actually played the 16th slot is nowhere.
(2) A ONE-OFF SUB. The owner had a sub a few weeks ago; the games are in the data (Billers records who actually played, which is why records come out right) but the schedule layer does not say the seat was covered.
(3) THE RULE. The league caps a sub at 7 appearances. Nothing counts them, so nobody can see who is at 5 or who is over.

WANTED (owner's words): put the real names of the people who subbed in, with an (S) or (Sub) beside them — for the standing Saturday sub and retroactively for anyone who subbed for the owner or anyone else.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE (for review, not settled):
- A sub is a SLOT FACT, never a second person. Add to the roster slot: sub_for (playerId of the member being covered, or null for a standing sub with no member behind it) and derive is_sub. The person in the seat is the person, with their own id — do not mint sub identities.
- GAMES ALWAYS BELONG TO WHOEVER PLAYED THEM. This is already true in Billers and must not change: a sub's wins are the sub's wins, on their own record and player page.
- WHAT THE (S) MARKS IS THE SEAT, NOT THE PERSON. It shows on the roster row, the draw and the court plate for that night. It does NOT stamp the sub's own player page or their ledger — they played a game, that is all it means about them.
- LEAGUE POINTS are the real open question and the reason the 7-cap exists: do a sub's results score for the absent member, for the sub, or for neither? Needs the league's actual rule text before anything is built. The cap only makes sense under one of those answers.
- THE CAP: count sub appearances per person per league season and surface it where the decision is made — a soft line on the roster row at 5-6 ('4th of 7 this season'), and a named consequence at 7 rather than a silent block. Same count feeds the 'I need a sub' flow.

BACKFILL: the historical sub appearances are inferable from the imported league data (a player in a night's lineup who is not on the league's member list). That inference is how the retroactive (S) gets applied — worth checking it against the Saturday 16th-slot case first, since that seat has NO member behind it and would otherwise look like an error rather than a standing sub.

Depends on nothing; touches the roster slot shape in pickleball-social/app/src/lib/firedata.ts (Slot / EventDoc), the roster row in app/event/[id].tsx, the draw and CourtPlate in src/components/kitchenline.tsx.
notes:
2026-08-13 THE RULE IS SETTLED AND THE APP WAS WRONG TWICE — both fixed and deployed (commit 0043bff).

(1) THE SEVEN IS POINTS PER GAME, NOT APPEARANCES. A seat played by a sub scores min(actual, 7) each game. Verified over 9 played weeks of both leagues with zero unexplained cells. The screen had been saying 'SUBBING · 3RD OF 7', i.e. asserting an appearance cap this league does not have; it now says 'SUBBING · THIS SEAT SCORES 7 A GAME AT MOST'.

(2) THE (S) WAS LANDING ON REGULARS. leagues/{id}/player_stats is keyed by the import's ids; after an identity merge the roster carries the SURVIVING id while player_stats still holds the imported one, so a straight lookup marked a man a sub in a league he had played every week of — it was on the owner's own Thursday row in production. leagueSeats now expands membership across mergedIntoPlayerId.

STILL OPEN, and the workbooks make it tractable now: sub_for. The scoresheets record who was covered (an X in the Sub column beside the MEMBER's row) and, for the open #16 seat, the sub's actual name in the row. The free-text SUBS block names 'Nive for #2' style pairs but is unreliable — Saturday wk2 X'd #5 (John Martin) and never named who covered him. Importing the X column + the #16 names into the schedule_event roster slots is what would let the app say WHO covered WHOM instead of only THAT a seat was covered. It would also replace the current not-in-player_stats inference, which is a guess where the workbook is a record.

ANSWERED: league points go to the SEAT, not the sub — the sub's own record keeps their games (they played them), while the seat takes min(actual,7) toward the standings.

title: Play's active face does not survive a reload — home() never returns live_session_id
description: firedata.home() hardcodes live_session_id: null (src/lib/firedata.ts, the return of home()), because sessions are still D1/worker-side while the rest of home is Firestore. Consequence after icl: the Play tab enters its ACTIVE face only from the local setSessionId() that startSession() returns — reload the page mid-morning and Play falls back to its inactive 'We're here — start' face while a live session is running, and starting again is the only visible path. Fix options: (a) have firedata.home() ask the worker for the caller's live session and fill live_session_id, (b) persist the live session id client-side next to the me token and rehydrate on mount, (c) move sessions to Firestore as part of the Billers fold-in. (b) is the cheap one and (a) is the correct one. Belongs with wr0's active-mode loop — scoring a game should advance the plate, which needs the session to still be there after a refresh.
close_reason: Superseded in practice: Play's active face for a league night is now local draw-walking state that rehydrates from lineupResults() — reopening Play mid-morning reads which games already have scores and resumes at the right one, no live_session_id needed. title: pickleball-social: a group invite 404s when the group has no upcoming event
description:

title: Navigation: the tab bar invariant is broken on the four highest-intent screens

- Propose lands you in the wrong tab with no way back. You enter from Schedule (schedule.tsx:58, :121); success does router.replace("/") (propose.tsx:75). You land on Home, the stack is replaced, and the night you just made is on the Schedule you left.

- A session has two endings: inside Play onDone refreshes in place (play.tsx:100); via /session/[id] it navigates to / (session/[id].tsx:29).
- /player is the most-pushed screen in the app (seven call sites) and has no lit scope, so it renders a floor with no you-are-here. Recommend giving it the Groups scope — a player is a person in your group. The null at tabbar.tsx:46 was a bug fix, not an IA decision.

FIXES: render TabBar in propose/start/record/edit and extend scopeOf (/propose and /edit -> schedule, /start -> groups, /record -> play). Do NOT add it to join/claim — those are pre-membership doors. Then propose.tsx:75 -> replace("/schedule"), start.tsx:98 -> replace("/group") then push propose, session/[id].tsx:29 -> Play not Home.

ALSO: /record is reachable from exactly ONE place — games.tsx:56, an empty state under Profile. Score entry is Play verb; today you can only find it when you have no games. Move the door into Play.

ALSO: standings/[leagueId] is scoped to Groups but only reachable from Profile (you.tsx:120), so the lit tab flips scope under you — and its content duplicates the table face inside event/[id].tsx:340-342. Same table, two screens, two owners. If Groups grows a table view, delete this route.

ALSO: 31 "as never" casts disable typed routes app-wide (filed separately) — the tabbar.tsx:73 one is the load-bearing case.

title: Content: one word per concept, and heads that stop changing identity when data is empty
description:
Content-design review 2026-08-13, against the products own standard (design/prototype-kitchenline/_BRIEF.md:57 "imperative second person, one sentence per screen").

1. HEADS CHANGE IDENTITY BETWEEN EMPTY AND FULL. On three of five tabs the headline reports ABSENCE when empty and names the PLACE when populated, and the note swaps the other way: Groups (group.tsx:247 vs :255), Schedule (schedule.tsx:54 vs :84), Play (play.tsx:121 vs :269). So a new user — the owner exact state — never sees the head the screen is actually built around. The headline should name the place and never move; only the note value changes. Emptiness is the Empty block job, which is already directly underneath saying the same thing twice.

2. THE OVER-LINE DOES EIGHT JOBS across the five tabs: a date, a count, a category, a method, a status, a source, a warning (you.tsx:282 "THIS CANNOT BE UNDONE"), a synonym for its own headline (you.tsx:140 "THE LEDGER"/"Recent"), and an aphorism (you.tsx:322 "DARK IS THE BASE"). ONE RULE: the note is the SCOPE of what is below — how many, of what, or as-of-when. Never a category name, never a warning, never an opinion.

3. "GAME" MEANS TWO OPPOSITE THINGS, TWO TAPS APART. schedule.tsx:56 "No games scheduled" means occasions; group.tsx:247 "No games recorded" means individual games to 11. Both are empty states a new user sees in one session. Canon: NIGHT = the scheduled occasion, GAME = one game to 11, GROUP = container, LEAGUE = a kind of group. SESSION must never be user-visible — it is the generator, not the thing (index.tsx:80 says "A session is on right now"). Kill "crew" as chrome (you.tsx:59) — it exists only because a user typed it into start.tsx:172 placeholder. Keep roster (people) and draw (printed games) as genuinely different; keep lineup and queue out of sight.
   CAVEAT FOR THE OWNER: the hero case is 6 AM, and the code says "rec morning" seven times. "Night" is factually wrong for it. Either accept it as idiom or prefer the concrete, since the app already prints the real weekday everywhere.

4. THREE EMPTY STATES ARE DEAD ENDS: you.tsx:195-199 "No games yet" has no action and is the profile of every new user; group.tsx:248-251 explains the denominator methodology to somebody who has never recorded a score; numbers.tsx:51-53 offers "Back" as its action. The template to copy is index.tsx:152-167 and group.tsx:114-119 — both name the state, say why it is normal, say who can fix it, and carry one action.

5. BUTTONS: three verbs for one destination — "Open the night" (index.tsx:142), "See the night" (play.tsx:321), "See who is in" (index.tsx:146); pick one. you.tsx confirm says "Erase me" under a trigger that says "Delete everything" — the confirm names a SMALLER scope than the trigger. play.tsx:458 "Tap both scores" is an instruction wearing ball paint, which means tappable; move it above the pad.

title: Typed routes are disabled app-wide by 31 'as never' casts
description:
Audit 2026-08-13. app.json:46-48 sets experiments.typedRoutes: true and .expo/types/router.d.ts is generated and current. Every route the app uses IS in that union, including templated ones. So none of the 31 'as never' casts are load-bearing — they only disable the check that would catch a typo'd path.

No currently-wrong path was found; the defect is the missing guardrail.

Highest value single change: app/src/components/tabbar.tsx:73 router.navigate(t.href as never) — TABS is typed { href: string }[], so a typo in the five-entry table would compile clean and ship a dead tab. Type href as Href and delete the cast.

Nine casts are on plain static literals TypeScript would accept verbatim: event/[id].tsx:110, index.tsx:81/215/222/223, you.tsx:189, join/[token].tsx:151, session/[id].tsx:29.

Also filed here: the tab bar is missing on propose.tsx, start.tsx, record.tsx and edit/[id].tsx, which contradicts the invariant stated in tabbar.tsx:8-12 (the two token doors are arguably fine, being pre-auth). scopeOf has no branch for /propose, /start, /record or /edit, so adding the bar there would light nothing until those are added.

title: Roster: guests are invisible, waitlist cannot be managed, addGuest is not idempotent
description:
Audit 2026-08-13, the residue after c8c7b15 fixed removal itself.

(1) GUESTS LOOK LIKE MEMBERS. subtitleFor (event/[id].tsx) only ever emits 'JOINED …' and never reads player.kind, though playerRef (firedata.ts:133) already sets kind and populates sponsor (:135-136) — and nothing renders sponsor. An organiser cannot tell who is a guest or whose guest they are. (The remove confirmation now distinguishes them; the roster row still does not.)

(2) WAITLISTED PEOPLE CANNOT BE REMOVED. The remove affordance lives only inside the court_views loop; the waitlist section renders bare RosterRows with no affordance. Pure UI omission — removal by slotId works fine for them.

(3) addGuest IS NOT IDEMPOTENT, contrary to three separate comments claiming it is: event/[id].tsx says 'idempotent on the name', api.ts takes _idempotencyKey and discards it, and firedata.ts unconditionally appends a new slot with a fresh synthetic id. A double-press adds the same person twice. api.ts also promises 'a relay channel so the person you brought is reachable'; the Firestore path creates no relay.

(4) The remove confirmation panel renders BELOW the entire roster and the organiser button block, so on a 16-person roster tapping REMOVE near the top puts the confirmation off-screen with no scroll-into-view — independently reproduces 'nothing happened'.

(5) No test files exist anywhere under app/. removeFromRoster had a nine-line doc comment describing behaviour it did not have, and nothing caught it.

title: No drilling events exist, and rec vs drilling is not expressible
description:
Owner 2026-08-13 said reminders are wanted for 'Rec and Drilling events'. Verified against production the same day: all ten schedule_events carry kind:'session' — the two city leagues, the four Whitney Sundays, everything. There is no drilling event and no field that could distinguish one.

Reminders currently qualify an event by NOT being a league (20-hex groupId heuristic, matching toEventView). Owner chose that deliberately: it covers Whitney today and picks up drilling automatically the day a drilling event is created, with no migration.

This issue is the follow-on IF rec and drilling ever need to behave differently — different reminder lead times, different copy, drilling not needing numbers confirmed the way a rec game does. That needs a real kind on schedule_events ('rec'|'drilling'|'league'), a backfill of the existing docs, and a creation path that sets it. Do not do it before there is a reason; the heuristic is honest until then.

title: contract:check fails and contract:sync would delete the app's Firestore-only fields
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while running quality gates for the ledger sub work; pre-existing, not introduced by it.

app/package.json has:
  contract:check  = diff -q ../server/src/contract.ts src/lib/contract.ts
  contract:sync   = cp ../server/src/contract.ts src/lib/contract.ts

contract:check currently FAILS. The drift is 17 lines, all ADDITIVE on the app side: EventDetail in app/src/lib/contract.ts carries group_name, is_league, is_organizer, week and lineup, each commented 'Firestore world only'. The server's copy does not have them.

So the sync the failing gate tells you to run is DESTRUCTIVE — cp goes server -> app, which would delete those five fields and break app/app/event/[id].tsx (is_league gates the whole table face; lineup draws the round-robin; week and group_name are in the appbar).

Decide which is true and fix accordingly:
(a) the Firestore fields belong in the shared contract -> add them server-side, then sync is safe again;
(b) they are genuinely app-only -> the check needs to compare only the shared surface, or the app should extend the contract type rather than hold a forked copy.

Until then the gate is noise: it fails every run and its own remedy is wrong.

title: Organisers need the fill line the players lost, plus which games need subs
description:
Owner 2026-08-13: the fill line ('15 in — court 4 needs 1 more') was removed from league nights because a player cannot act on it and seeing it weekly makes the app read as broken. But it is real information for whoever organises, and the owner asked for it to come back as an admin function — specifically so they can see WHICH GAMES NEED SUBS.

Shape: on a league night, for an organiser only, the short seats and the games those seats appear in — because a seat short on a round robin does not cost one game, it costs the seven games that seat is drawn into, and it costs the three other people on each of those courts. The draw already knows which games a seat is in, so the list is derivable with no new data.

Ties into c2o: a seat that is short and a seat that is subbed are the same question asked a week apart.

title: The other ~18 imported leagues still have import-timestamp playedAt
description:
skk fixed the two leagues the owner has workbooks for (Saturday Adv 4.0-4.5 Police Memorial, Thursday Adv 4.0-4.5 Bill Briare). Every other vegas_import league still carries the import moment as playedAt and a null date, so recent-ordering, the night-grouped ledger, wins-after-a-loss and head-to-head streaks remain arbitrary for them.

The tool is done and league-parameterised: scripts/apply_vegas_week_dates.ts in the Billers repo. Each league needs one file, pickleball_stats/data/imports/vegas/{leagueId}_week_dates.json, holding {leagueId, leagueName, note, sessionDates: [...]}.

Getting the dates: (a) the city workbook for that league if the owner has it — the DATE cell on each week's scoresheet; (b) back-extrapolation from any schedule_event whose title names its week ('... — Week 6 of 7'), since these leagues run weekly at a fixed time — verified exact against both known leagues; (c) the league doc's season field plus the city's published schedule.

(b) needs no new input and would cover every league that has any schedule_event, so it is the cheap first pass. Two anchors in the same league should be checked 7 days apart before trusting it.

title: The organiser check for removal is client-side only
description:
app/event/[id].tsx gates 'Take somebody off' on EventView.is_organizer, which firedata derives from schedule_events.organizerPlayerId. That is a SCREEN gate, not a rule gate: firestore.rules allows any signed-in caller to update an event's roster ('allow update: if isAdmin() || (isSignedIn() && ...affectedKeys().hasOnly([roster, rosterPlayerIds, updatedAt, confirmDeadline, note, title]))'), so anybody who can reach the API can take anybody off any roster.

That rule is also what makes join/drop/addGuest work without a server, so tightening it needs care. Options: (a) a callable for removal specifically, leaving self-service writes alone; (b) a rules predicate that allows a roster diff only when the slots changing are the caller's own or the caller is the event's organizer — expressible but fiddly against an array-of-maps; (c) accept it for a trusted-group product and write the decision down.

Not urgent for a private league app; do not ship a public one without deciding.

title: [bug] The Playoffs lineup has each game duplicated onto two courts
description:
Seen in schedule_events/baba19eb5730b334a1b7-20260829 ('Saturday Adv 4.0-4.5 — Playoffs', lineupSource 'Playoffs'). Game 1 court 1 and game 1 court 3 list the IDENTICAL pairing (Ronald P & Lawrence G v Melissa L & Brian J); same for court 2 and court 4, and the pattern repeats through all 7 games. Every game appears twice.

Either the playoff scoresheet genuinely runs the same matchup on two courts (possible but unlikely) or the importer double-wrote courts 3 and 4 from courts 1 and 2. Consequences if it is an import artifact: the draw screen shows 28 games where there are 14, Play's active-mode loop will walk the same matchup twice and ask for its score twice, and the derived doc id (gp-{eventId}-g{n}-c{n}) will happily write both as separate matches — doubling everybody's playoff record.

Check the source scoresheet before the 29th. Only the playoffs event is affected; Weeks 6 and 7 have distinct pairings per court.

title: Group membership needs a callable — groups.memberIds is admin-write-only
description:
firedata.joinGroup() writes groups/{id}.memberIds via arrayUnion and CANNOT WORK: firestore.rules has 'match /groups/{groupId} { allow write: if isAdmin(); }'. It is dead code today — nothing calls it since the invite door joins a night instead.

Consequence: a group with nothing on the calendar cannot be joined at all (the invite door says so honestly), and membership is really 'you are on a roster of one of its nights', so dropping out of the only scheduled night silently drops you out of the group.

Fix: a joinGroupByInvite({groupId}) callable in Billers that validates and does the arrayUnion with the Admin SDK. Do NOT relax the rule to let a signed-in user add themselves — groups are world-readable (allow read: if true), so that would let anybody join any group by id and would break §4.2 (the group has no address). The invite has to be checked server-side for the door to mean anything.

title: Apply migration 0003 to production D1
description: 0003_roster_declined.sql (adds 'declined' to roster_entry.state) is applied locally but NOT on the remote pickleball database — remote has 2 of 3 migrations. Any code path writing state='declined' will abort in prod until 'npx wrangler d1 migrations apply pickleball --remote' is run from server/. Low risk but needs a moment when no writes are in flight.

title: iOS list rows should navigate on tap instead of being re-stated as giant buttons
description: Cold review 2026-08-12, Apple-bar gap #2: groups/1 renders a nav list then adds a full-width OPEN THURSDAY ADV button duplicating a row; native iOS trusts the row + chevron affordance. The deck's right-edge-chevron grammar exists (goes-somewhere rows); the double-writing is where the 'over the top' feeling now comes from after the copy cut. Sweep every screen that states an action twice (row + button) and keep one. Also comp-league/5 'Settled' title immediately repeated as section header.

title: Ledger jargon has no glossary: held / deferred / counted, '61 of 77', '2-3-2' chip
description: Cold review 2026-08-12: you/1 says '68 games counted · 2 held'; profile/1 adds 'deferred'; 'held' is only explained on profile/1 and 'deferred' nowhere. home/2's '61 of 77' has no unit (points won of points played) and the '2-3-2' chip never says the third number is level games. Also 'ANSWER NEEDED' (groups/1) vs 'THEY NEED AN ANSWER' (home/1) — same state, two phrasings. Needs one terms-and-formats table applied everywhere; overlaps pickleball-telegram-bot-h8g (points labels).
notes: 2026-08-12: partially resolved by the natural-language pass — 'games counted' is now 'games', the 2-3-2 chip now reads 2W · 3L · 2 TIED, draw vocabulary unified to 'tied'. Still open: 'held'/'deferred' only explained on profile/1, '61 of 77' still unitless.

title: Button labels aren't verbs: ALL SEVEN / EVERY GAME / EVERYTHING / SEND IT need one verb-first naming pass
description: Cold review of the polished journeys deck (2026-08-12), top Apple-bar gap: roughly half the CTAs need the surrounding screen to decode. The same drill-down (full game history) is labelled ALL SEVEN (home/2), EVERY GAME (you/1) and EVERYTHING (profile/1); drill-friends/2's SEND IT has no visible recipient or channel; rec-friends/4's SEND IT THROUGH JOHN is uninterpretable in 2 seconds (note: that label is register-protected from the copy audit — commit bde6f7fe says it states what actually happens — so this is a design reconciliation, not a mechanical rename). One verb-first naming table applied deck-wide. 'Game 4' on comp-rr/4 was already fixed to 'Start game 4'.
notes: 2026-08-12 natural-language pass applied (pickleball-social 59a6f9b): PLAYING / I NEED A SUB, Who's in band, Confirm score / Fix the score / Set up a game, View all everywhere, tied not level, 68 games not games counted, group-kind pills (LEAGUE/REC·SOCIAL/OPEN PLAY/DRILLS), 19 CTAs shortened. Remaining design work on this issue: wire 'I need a sub' into the sub-ask flow (currently still writes declined and stops, per D28); decide LET JOHN TELL ME vs the register-protected 'Send it through John'; the visual confirm affordance (tick / row highlight) the client sketched lives with h48.

title: Score-entry rows need button affordance (winner preselect), not just the 'Who won' label
description: Copy audit verdict REDESIGN on the rec-friends score-entry screen: the seclbl said 'Tap a name — winners first' because the three name rows don't look tappable and no side is preselected. The label is now 'Who won'; the real fix is rendering the rows as controls in the deck's offset-block-edge button grammar with the reporter's winning side preselected. In design/journeys/index.html, the score-entry screens under rec-friends (and their organiser/disputes siblings). Related: 4s2 (no text input drawn anywhere).

title: No organiser view of the round robin: no draw preview, no pinned pairing, no seeding
description: From a 5.0 persona who runs a 12-16 player invitational round robin and a monthly ladder on a spreadsheet with her own rotation algorithm. She said the rotation quality itself matches her spreadsheet - comp-rr/4's 56 distinct pairings with zero repeats, 119 of 120 possible pairs over five weeks, checkable rather than asserted. What is missing is her. comp-rr/1 gives one button, 'Start game 1', and comp-rr/2 shows the draw already committed: no preview, no regenerate, no way to pin a pairing she wants tested. No seeding anywhere - court 1 is an ordinal, not the top court, so 4.0s and 5.0s shuffle flat, which she called the loudest complaint she would get. Rotation is also the only format; fixed_partners is a reserved enum with no generator. Named as the ONE thing that flips her verdict from 'part of it' to yes. Three smaller gaps from the same review: comp-rr/6 draws exactly one sitter when 13-14 players means two or three every game; no screen shows a per-player sit-out count, so the fairness rule is stated but not auditable; and groups/4 offers audience 'Just who I ask' while no name picker exists on any screen, so her weekly 16-of-30 invite list cannot be expressed.
acceptance_criteria: An organiser previews, adjusts and commits a draw; seeding is expressible; sit-out counts are visible per player; the 'just who I ask' picker exists.

title: The product computes a rating and refuses to use it for matching
description: Independently reached by a 5.0 tournament player and a never-played beginner from opposite ends, which is why it is worth recording. The 5.0: nothing in 102 screens helps him find a game at his level; entry/6 says 'all welcome', rec-open says 'all levels welcome', comp-friends/2 offers Competitive/Chill/Drills and no level, and organiser/2 sorts subs by acceptances. Level lives only in group NAMES. The beginner: 'Thursday Adv 4.0-4.5' on home/5 and dropping/2 was the single string that would stop him turning up - '4.0-4.5 of what?' - and no screen anywhere explains what the scale means, where the floor is, or where 'fine' sits. So the same undrawn concept simultaneously blocks the strongest player from finding a good game and the weakest from daring to join a normal one. Note this is a deliberate-looking absence, not an oversight: rating-based matching has real social costs and D17's people-search rules constrain it. It needs a recorded decision either way rather than silence.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on rating-based level signalling, and if yes, an event states its level in something other than its name.

title: The uncertainty band is required by INV-9 and drawn on no screen
description: From the 5.0 tournament-player review of design/journeys. Rating.uncertainty exists in schema.md and INV-9 states a provisional rating is 'drawn as a band, not a point'. No screen draws one - not you/1, not profile/1, not even you/2 where the player has one game of ten. A 4.12 over 68 games and a 4.12 over 11 games render identically, which is precisely the distinction the field exists to express. Related from the same review: RatingEvent.explanation is capped at 'rung 2 - never publish coefficients', so you/3 ranks inputs and withholds weights; the reviewer's word for that was 'inspectable, not auditable' - he cannot recompute the 62% expected-win figure the screen shows him. And schema.md badges seeded_from_dupr as 'Seeded' until match 10; that badge is on no screen either.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional ratings render as a band; the Seeded badge appears where a DUPR seed is in effect.

title: A league season has no playoff, and no screen sets the response deadline
description: From a league-organiser persona re-review of design/journeys, after she said she would switch her league over for weeks 1-7 and put week 8 back on paper. Two gaps. (1) groups/5 creates a recurring event with '4 weeks / keep going / a season', and groups/3 shows a 'Playoffs - top 8' row that nothing builds; both real Las Vegas leagues in data/ are 7 weeks then a bracket seeded from the standings. (2) groups/2 and organiser/1 both reference an answer-by-Wednesday deadline and no screen sets it; Event.roster_closes_at exists in schema.md and is drawn nowhere. Also noted and smaller: no screen anywhere shows how a score number is actually typed - organiser/4, disputes/2 and comp-league/4 all draw the numbers pre-filled with no keypad, stepper or field.
acceptance_criteria: A season can be built with a playoff seeded from standings; roster_closes_at is set on a screen; and one score-entry screen shows the actual input.
notes: 2026-08-12: score keypad/text-input stays out of the polish pass by scope agreement (polish existing screens only). The 'Tap a name — winners first' label was reduced to 'Who won'; the row-affordance redesign is filed separately.

title: An organiser removing a member is the last thing the product does TO somebody, and it is undrawn
description: Named by a UX re-review as the single most important remaining gap in design/journeys, after signing off on everything else. groups/7 asserts removal is organiser-only in every invite_mode, D10 calls it irreversible (adding a person is reversible, removing one is not), groups/8 draws only voluntary leaving, and path-organiser ends on the screen that names the power without ever drawing its use. It is the only remaining case where the product does something TO a person rather than for them, which makes it the one most in need of the care the rest of the set gets: what the organiser sees before confirming, what the removed person sees, whether they are told at all, and the fact that they may still write a Score for a match in progress they are a participant in, because authorisation for score entry is participation and never membership. Ranked after it: failure states (no offline entry, no lost race on start-round, no expired link in 102 screens), capacity overflow (rec-friends/3 insists 'not a waiting list' and person 17 of 16 at open play has no screen), and editing a proposal.
acceptance_criteria: Removal is drawn from both sides, and the removed person's surviving rights are on the screen rather than only in the contract.
close_reason: Shipped in commit d53570a. The organiser gets one power over somebody else, behind a switch: 'Take somebody off' reveals a TAKE OFF affordance per roster row, and choosing one names the consequence before anything happens ('the queue closes up behind them, exactly as if they had dropped out themselves; anyone they brought comes off too; they can join again from the link they came in on'). firedata.removeFromRoster() tombstones the slot the same way that person's own drop would, so nothing in the record says they were removed rather than left — the deck's rule that the product never marks somebody with a fault. EventView gained is_organizer (Firestore-world only). Prompted by a real hole: the owner joined via an invite in a private window, and the anonymous identity was unreachable afterwards, so the roster carried a name nobody could shift.

title: Nothing in the product knows that time has passed — no dormancy, no rating staleness, no quiet way back
description: From a returning-player persona reviewing design/journeys — played 3x a week for four months, tore a calf, six months out, now cleared. Her findings. (1) After six months the first screen is home/6 'Quiet week', which is honest and cold: the app thinks she had a quiet WEEK. Nothing anywhere says it has been a while. (2) you/1 shows 4.12 with a +0.06 delta from a match in February, presented as current, with no date and no staleness marker — and profile/2 shows that number to everyone she shares a group with. She wants it greyed with 'last played 12 Feb' or held pending a few games back. (3) The only acknowledgement of elapsed time anywhere in 118 screens is the 'Last played 6 Aug' subtitle on a groups/1 row. (4) home/4 draws a FORWARD gap as a tappable band; there is no backwards equivalent. (5) No season archive — if her league rolled over, her 257 and her 13th place are simply on no screen. (6) Worst: the only way back in is groups/4, which broadcasts a proposal to fifteen people after six months of silence. There is no quiet re-entry — no way to take an open slot on something already happening. Her verdict: 'the app never noticed I left, so it cannot notice I am back.' Note the product is right not to record absence as a fault (dropping/2 deliberately stores no counter); this is about elapsed time, not reliability.
acceptance_criteria: A returning-user state exists, rating staleness is visible to the owner and to viewers, and there is a way back in that does not require proposing.
close_reason: Closed

title: No organiser operational view, and no subs flow
description: From the league-organiser persona review of design/journeys (16 players, 4 courts, 7 games, 7 weeks, currently a clipboard and an Excel workbook). The only organiser screen in 111 is groups/6 Settings - invite mode, requires_recording, who can remove - which is governance, not operations. She needs one board at 8:40pm with a phone in one hand: who has answered and who has not, which courts have a score in and which do not. comp-league/3 shows all four courts but it is a player's screen. Separately, comp-league/1 has a 'Send a sub' button that goes nowhere and no sub flow exists anywhere; finding subs when two drop on the day is her second-worst pain of the week. She also noted that availability shows a COUNT (14 of 16) and never the two names who have not answered, so she is back to texting blind, and that no screen anywhere shows how a score number is actually typed - comp-league/4 draws the score pre-filled with no keypad, stepper or field.
acceptance_criteria: An organiser night-view exists; a sub request flow exists or the button is removed; availability names the silent; a score-entry screen shows the actual input.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing is designed for the beginner's day one, and 'the kitchen' actively misleads
description: From the beginner persona review of design/journeys - nine weeks into playing, invited by a friend, no league experience. Three concrete findings. (1) There is no beginner state of the You tab: you/1 is John with 109 games, and nobody has drawn what a person sees on day one. Her rating is 'withheld' but that word only appears in the state panel, never on a screen - so she sees other people's numbers and an absence where hers should be, and an unexplained absence reads as 'not good enough yet' louder than a small number would. (2) 'In the kitchen - can't be changed' was misread for a full minute by the one reviewer who actually knows the sport: the kitchen is the non-volley zone, and borrowing a familiar word for an unfamiliar meaning is worse than a new word. A UX review reached the same conclusion independently. Recommend 'Settled - can't be changed' in copy, keeping kitchen paint as the visual zone. (3) 'Your spot doesn't move. People ahead of you can drop; you only ever go up' was written to reassure and does the opposite - it tells a beginner there is an order and she is near the bottom of it. Also: rec-friends/6 pre-selects the reader as the winner, which she called mortifying, and rec-friends/5 leads with 'Singles - two of you play', which excludes the third person with no way to say who sits.
acceptance_criteria: A day-one You screen exists; the withheld rating explains itself on screen at the moment of joining; the kitchen copy decision is recorded either way.
close_reason: Closed

title: api.md has no section 8.2, and notification categories are never enumerated
description: Found while designing the push-permission screen for design/journeys (rec-friends/4). api.md section 8 jumps straight from 8.1 (the reachability ladder and the relay) to 8.3 (push registration). There is no 8.2. Separately, 8.4 says 'Defaults are logistics-on, engagement-off' and PUT /notification-preferences takes a 'category' field, but no catalogue of categories exists anywhere in the contract. This matters beyond tidiness: the consent copy on the permission screen promises 'only about games you are in, nothing else, ever', and that promise is only honest if logistics-only is genuinely the default and the category list is closed. OQ-23 (court_broke unmutable while on a roster) also references categories that are not defined.
acceptance_criteria: api.md gains a section 8.2 defining the notification category enum, which categories are logistics vs engagement, and which are unmutable while on a roster; the permission-screen copy in design/journeys is checked against it.

title: declined -> in keeps the original position, letting a decliner jump the queue
description: Opened by D28 (2026-08-11). RosterEntry has a UNIQUE index on (event_id, player_id) and position is NOT NULL and write-once, so changing your mind is a state transition on one row and the original position survives. Somebody who declined at position 3 and re-enters at 7pm therefore sits ahead of four people who said yes in between. Options: a nullable re-entry position, a separate re_entered_at ordering key, or accept it and say so on the screen. Note dropped -> in has carried the identical problem since v1 and was never decided; declining makes it far more likely to be hit because declining is cheap and dropping is not.
acceptance_criteria: A rule is recorded in the decision register, schema.md's RosterEntry cascade invariants reflect it, and a schema test covers re-entry ordering.
close_reason: Resolved by the move to Firestore rosters, and the rule is now recorded. The bug was a D1 schema artifact: RosterEntry had UNIQUE(event_id, player_id) with a write-once NOT NULL position, so re-entry was a state transition on one row and the original position survived. The Firestore roster is an ordered array of slots with 'out' TOMBSTONES LEFT IN PLACE (firedata.ts drop()), and join() appends a NEW slot at the end after checking only non-out slots for a duplicate. Rank is the index among active slots, so somebody who declined at 3 and re-enters at 7pm lands behind everyone who said yes in between. THE RULE: re-entry goes to the back of the queue; the tombstone holds no claim on the old position. Same for dropped -> in, which had carried the identical problem since v1.

Collapses claim+join into ONE tap. PREREQS: bot must be group admin with can_invite_users, and the webhook must be re-registered with allowed_updates including 'chat_member' (verified: NOT sent by default). Product vocabulary idea from the Kitchen Line (P1) direction study, 2026-08-06: map the sport's own non-volley zone ('the kitchen') onto the app's immutability rule. Pickleball already has a named zone where a different rule applies; the product already has locked state (played rounds, confirmed courts, recorded history are immutable per decision D04 and BRIEF 4.1). Naming the locked/no-edit state 'the kitchen' gives the app native sport vocabulary instead of generic UI language. Also from P1: 'every score is two sides across a net, never a hyphen on one line' as a layout rule. See pickleball-social/design/direction-P1-court.html.

Design constraint discovered via the Cold Issue (Bond 2050) direction study, 2026-08-06: a player's name must never be rendered next to a fault/error colour or failure language. Dropping out early is the behaviour the drop-and-cascade mechanic depends on; any visual language that renders a withdrawal as failure (red, 'COMPROMISED', broken-streak graphics) discourages the single most valuable social behaviour in the product. Applies to every design direction. This is foundation #8 (NOT #7 — a numbering swap propagated from _BRIEF.md was corrected everywhere on 2026-08-12; canonical numbering is prototype-kitchenline/index.html: #7 = list is the record, #8 = no name beside a fault colour).

Design constraint from the direction studies, 2026-08-06: the ordered 1-8 roster queue must always be printed as a numbered list, no matter what spatial metaphor a design uses. Rings, panel grids and 2x2 court blocks cannot encode sequence, and sequence is the product's core mechanic. The graphic is the summary; the list is the record; if they disagree the list wins.
